financials_interim.notes: No extraction issues (verified via EPS 21.70 = 510,999k / 23,545,000 shares). Single set of statements -- 'the Company', not a Group/Company split -- following the amalgamation of subsidiaries Millennium Multibreeder Farms (Pvt) Ltd and Ceylon Pioneer Poultry Breeders Ltd into TAFL effective 1 January 2026 (TAFL is the surviving amalgamated entity). The 2025 comparative column in this filing represents the FORMER Group's results (i.e. TAFL + those two subsidiaries pre-amalgamation), included for comparability of scope even though the corporate structure changed -- so this YoY comparison is like-for-like on business scope but not on legal entity structure. No interest-bearing borrowings (bank loans or leases) are disclosed on this balance sheet -- short_term_borrowings/long_term_borrowings left blank, not zero-by-omission. finance_costs entered as 0 since the P&L shows a net 'Interest income / (finance cost)' line that was net positive (49) this quarter; finance_income (207,064) is interest income before netting the small finance cost against it. Cash flow not entered: filing discloses only six-month cumulative cash flow, not the quarter in isolation, and no Q1 2026 figures are on file to derive Q2 alone.

interim_updates.note_text: Three Acre Farms (now the amalgamated entity following the 1 January 2026 absorption of Millennium Multibreeder Farms and Ceylon Pioneer Poultry Breeders) posted revenue of Rs.1.86bn for Q2 2026 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 51% YoY against the former Group's Rs.1.23bn, with gross margin surging from 2.4% to 29.9%. PAT rose from Rs.108.6mn to Rs.511.0mn (+370%). Per the company's own quarterly review, this reflects both higher sales volumes and higher average selling prices for Broiler Day-Old Chicks, which outweighed cost pressure from inflation, Rupee depreciation, and higher raw material and energy costs -- the same input-cost narrative as parent company Ceylon Grain Elevators' own Q2 2026 filing. For H1 2026, revenue was Rs.3.52bn (+30% YoY) and profit Rs.925.1mn (+102% YoY).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one (e.g. 31 March 2026) has been collected for TAFL. Cash flow is not entered into financial_statements for this period because the filing discloses only six-month cumulative cash flow, not the quarter in isolation. No interest-bearing borrowings are disclosed on this balance sheet, so short/long-term borrowings and debt-based ratios are not applicable for this symbol, not a missing-data gap.
interim_updates.takeaway: An even sharper version of parent Ceylon Grain Elevators' Q2 story: DOC pricing power more than offset input-cost inflation, turning a low-single-digit gross margin a year ago into nearly 30% this quarter. Worth remembering the YoY comparison spans a corporate restructuring (amalgamation), not just organic growth, though the business scope is comparable.
operational_highlights: Revenue Rs.1.86bn for Q2 2026, up 51% YoY; gross margin surged from 2.4% to 29.9%
PAT Rs.511.0mn, up 370% YoY (Rs.108.6mn a year earlier); PBT up 390% (Rs.154.0mn to Rs.754.3mn)
H1 2026: revenue Rs.3.52bn (+30% YoY), profit Rs.925.1mn (+102% YoY)

Millennium Multibreeder Farms (Pvt) Ltd and Ceylon Pioneer Poultry Breeders Ltd were amalgamated into TAFL effective 1 January 2026; the 2025 comparative reflects the former Group's results for scope comparability
57.21% owned by Ceylon Grain Elevators PLC, whose own Q2 2026 filing describes the same DOC demand/pricing dynamics
key_drivers: Management's own commentary (shared with parent Ceylon Grain Elevators' filing): higher sales volumes and average selling prices for Broiler Day-Old Chicks outweighed cost pressure from high inflation, Rupee depreciation, higher raw material prices and increased energy costs
Gross margin expansion (2.4% to 29.9%) is the overwhelming driver of the profit swing -- cost of sales grew only 9% while revenue grew 51%, indicating pricing/mix gains rather than volume alone

The YoY comparison spans TAFL's absorption of two former subsidiaries (amalgamation effective 1 January 2026) -- the 2025 comparative is restated to the former Group's results, so this is a like-for-like business-scope comparison, not a pure standalone-company trend
